message_source_quote: Inspired by Raman et al. (2026) White-Bear Steering, but built from entirely self-authored prompts, with different concepts, carrier sentences, and wording — not WSB's `directed_modulation` items — with the dose tuned on the fit split.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance vector from WSB's directed_modulation items lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 on this model. This submission applies the same principle but builds the direction from entirely self-authored prompts with different concepts, carrier sentences and wording, and tunes the dose on fit.
rationale: Both the write-up and the closing message name Raman et al. (2026) / White-Bear Steering explicitly, describe the method as applying the same think/don't-think stance-contrast principle, and claim novelty via entirely self-authored prompts (different concepts, carriers, wording) rather than WSB's directed_modulation items, with the dose tuned on the fit split. The two documents agree on the credit level, the overlap with the source, and the novelty claim, so there is no material difference between them.
